1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing, though it is not identifiable as a specifically dyslexia-friendly font.

2.why: No italics or all-caps text appear anywhere; all copy is short sentence-case lines rather than dense blocks.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single column with large inputs and buttons that fit a mobile viewport, though the developer-style 'Logs' panel adds some clutter.

4.why: Instructions are one short plain sentence each, e.g. 'Sign in first. Then we will help you add your authenticator.'

5.why: Expected input is exemplified through placeholders such as 'Example: 123456' for the code and 'name@example.com' for email.

6.why: No screen contains more than a couple of short sentences; the user never has to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears on any screen, and the authenticator/backup-code steps where long secrets would occur are never reached (screenshot marked INCOMPLETE).

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is shown anywhere; the flow stalls at the identity check and the authenticator setup screen is never displayed.

9.why: Standard email, password and code inputs are used, which browsers can typically autofill, but explicit autofill or password-manager support cannot be confirmed from the images.

10.why: A 'Step X of 4' banner and a bold full-width blue primary button mark each step, though on the code screen the leftover 'Send code' button also carries the focus highlight.

11.why: The verification screen simultaneously presents 'Send code', 'Check code' and 'Send a new code', so more than one action is offered at once.

12.why: Banners plainly confirm each result and the next step, e.g. 'Signed in. Next, check it is you.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.'

13.why: A 'Send a new code' button allows re-requesting and retrying with no penalty shown, though no reveal/hide toggle for codes is visible.

14.why: The error 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.' states the problem and the fix in neutral, non-blaming wording.

15.why: No countdowns, timers, or auto-advancing elements appear, and messages such as 'Enter it when you are ready' explicitly remove time pressure.
